claims.text: The 187 article graphs hold 2,348 nodes and 2,381 edges, 12.6 nodes each.
claims.quote: The 187 article graphs hold 2,348 nodes and 2,381 edges, 12.6 nodes each.

claims.text: Of 2,286 distinct node labels, 48 appear in more than one article's graph.
claims.quote: 2,286 distinct labels, and 48 of them appear in more than one article's graph.

claims.text: The articles carry 672 tags and 401 are used once; 379 raw tags are still unmapped.
claims.quote: The articles carry 672 tags and 401 are used once.

claims.text: The site says a node takes its meaning from what it is connected to, and its own article graphs connect to almost nothing outside their article.
claims.quote: its own article graphs connect to almost nothing outside their article

claims.text: The outside sources in the graphs are 753 links across 258 domains, none carrying a date.
claims.quote: 753 of them, across 258 domains, github.com first with 57

claims.text: The owner's memo asks for a second reading of every article from the bottom up, with the dimensions above allowed to emerge rather than drawn in advance.
claims.quote: let the dimensions above appear on their own rather than be drawn in advance

claims.text: A new dimension is needed where the ontology and taxonomy change; a layer with the same vocabulary further away is the same level seen from further away.
claims.quote: The moment the ontology and taxonomy change, that is where a new dimension is needed.

claims.text: The owner remembers rUv mapping his own writings and concepts onto two hemispheres, like a brain, and wants the same done here.
claims.quote: mapped his own writings, concepts and publications onto two hemispheres, like a brain

claims.text: Two articles: this brief with predictions before any article is read the second way, and a second comparing expectations with what happened.
claims.quote: This one first, with the brief, my expectations and my predictions, written before any article is read the second way

claims.text: Two earlier readings exist for five articles: the Librarian's 662 anchored items and the Cartographer's 45 concepts and 78 edges.
claims.quote: catalogued 662 items with the sentence each came from, and a Cartographer turned those into 45 concepts and 78 edges

claims.text: This run anchors every claim to its sentence as the Librarian did, but stops at twelve to thirty-five claims per article rather than every noun.
claims.quote: twelve to thirty-five claims per article, not a hundred and thirty

claims.text: The grammar is five rules: every edge a verb with a named inverse, no generic association edge, properties carry data not meaning, supersede never delete, never render the whole graph.
claims.quote: The grammar is graphs.sgit.ai's and the fractal graphs article's, and it is five rules.

claims.text: The build will not invent a level: where a layer has the vocabulary of the layer below it is the same dimension at less resolution, and where it changes a new dimension is named with the edge that joins the two.
claims.quote: So the build will not invent a level.

claims.text: Each article gets one JSON file holding its claims with kind, section, verbatim quote, the names and concepts they are about, edges between claims, names, concepts, dated sources and dates.
claims.quote: Each article gets one file

claims.text: The validator looks for every quote in the twin and refuses an unknown kind, a verb outside the list, an unregistered name or concept, an em-dash and the ladder word.
claims.quote: looks for every quote in the twin and fails the file if it is not there

claims.text: The worked example, Every link points back, came out at 25 claims, 17 edges, two names, six concepts and two dates, and passes the validator.
claims.quote: 25 claims (ten facts, five data points, four proposals, four limits, one hypothesis, one decision), 17 edges, two names, six concepts, two dates

claims.text: The registries are seeded with 75 concepts and 137 names before the run.
claims.quote: The registries are seeded, not empty.

claims.text: The order of the run is deliberate: this article first, then readers in batches of about ten, then the merge, then a deterministic derivation, then the second article.
claims.quote: The order matters for honesty, so here it is.

claims.text: The readers are many and the validator is one, the wire's split between the model that proposes and the code that checks.
claims.quote: The readers are many and the validator is one

claims.text: A dimension is a layer with its own ontology, its own node types and verbs; a count such as gravity, and a cluster, are queries within a dimension, not new ones.
claims.quote: A dimension is a layer with its own ontology: its own node types and its own verbs.

claims.text: The editor's six topics, five desks with 44 subjects, eleven series, nine formats, one section and five personas are the control the clusters and peaks are scored against.
claims.quote: The editor's layers are the control.

claims.text: A peak is a node with high gravity that also bridges clusters: a company, a standard, an idea several desks share, an area a persona would start from.
claims.quote: A peak is where people arrive.

claims.text: Five drawings, in order: the two-way cut as lobes, a three-dimensional turn on a canvas with no library, the altitude diagram, the peaks as a ridge, and the births on a date axis.
claims.quote: The drawings, in the order I will attempt them.

claims.text: Prediction 1: 187 articles will yield 3,500 to 5,500 claims, with data points 20 to 30%, hypotheses 8 to 15%, limits 15 to 25%.
claims.quote: 187 articles will yield between 3,500 and 5,500 claims.

claims.text: Prediction 2: at least 300 ids will appear in two or more articles, and at least 60% of claims will be about something another article is also about.
claims.quote: At least 300 concept and name ids will appear in two or more articles

claims.text: Prediction 3: five dimensions will hold their own types and verbs, concepts and names will be one dimension, and at least one unlisted dimension will be needed.
claims.quote: Five will hold their own types and verbs: the claims, the names, the sources, time, and the editor's layers.

claims.text: Prediction 4: six to nine clusters; Agents & policy will split in two and Vaults & method will merge with Graphs & knowledge.
claims.quote: The concept graph will fall into six to nine clusters.

claims.text: Prediction 5: the cut will put control on one side and the record on the other, with the behaviour policy and the vault as the bridge, and the control side the larger at 55 to 65% of articles.
claims.quote: The control side will be the larger, 55 to 65% of the articles.

claims.text: Prediction 6: the top names will include Claude and Claude Code, sgit, RiskMandate, Anthropic, GitHub, the EU AI Act and OWASP; the top concepts the behaviour policy, the vault, provenance, fractal semantic graphs and the reading meter.
claims.quote: At least one peak will be something I would not have listed.

claims.text: Prediction 7: most concepts with gravity will have been born in September or the first week of October, and the 30 newest articles will add under three new concepts each.
claims.quote: The 30 newest articles will introduce under three new concepts each on average

claims.text: Prediction 8: 1,000 to 1,400 references across 300 or more domains, at least a third dated to the day, with github.com and Anthropic's documentation leading.
claims.quote: Between 1,000 and 1,400 references across 300 or more domains, at least a third dated to the day

claims.text: Prediction 9: at least 70% of each desk's articles will land in one or two clusters, the publishers' section in one, each persona in one or two.
claims.quote: At least 70% of each desk's articles will land in one or two clusters

claims.text: Prediction 10: the validator will refuse at least 5% of claims on first pass, at least 10% of proposed new concepts will duplicate a registry id, and the extraction will cost more model time than the writing of any article here.
claims.quote: The validator will refuse at least 5% of claims on first pass for a quote that is not word for word.

claims.text: The same brief is kept as a README in the repository, read by every later run, with each run's expectations added to it.
claims.quote: It is what the next run reads before it starts, and each run adds its own expectations to the end of it.

claims.text: No article has been read the second way yet; every number is the baseline and every claim about emergence a prediction.
claims.quote: No article has been read the second way yet.

claims.text: The hemispheres picture rests on the owner's memory of rUv's map; the page could not be found, so there is no link.
claims.quote: The hemispheres picture is from memory.

claims.text: The readers are the same model as the writer; no second model checks the files in this run.
claims.quote: The readers are the same model as the writer.

claims.text: The registries are seeds chosen from counts and the writing guide, not from reading every article.
claims.quote: 75 concepts and 137 names, chosen from counts and the writing guide, not from reading every article

claims.text: This is one run; the memo expects a couple, so the clusters and peaks after one are a first shape, not the shape.
claims.quote: the clusters and peaks after one are a first shape, not the shape
